newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ share market closes easier in featureless trade.
newsitem.headline: NZ share market closes easier in featureless trade.

text.p: * Light trade seen for next few days due to U.S. holidays
* Political impasse also putting some investors off
New Zealand's share market closed easier on Thursday in a featureless session that is likely to be repeated over the next few days.

Brokers said that with the U.S. going into the Thanksgiving holiday, trade was likely to be slim until Tuesday. Also pegging some investors back was the political impasse which looks likely to stretch into the seventh week since the election.
The NZSE-40 index fell 10.47 to 2346.35 on volume of NZ$40 million.
The main falls included Telecom, three cents to $7.43, Lion Nathan four to $3.64, Carter Holt Harvey four to $3.23 and Brierley one to $1.26.

Brokers said news that Lion's Chief Operating Officer Kevin Roberts was departing the company was mixed. It showed further disruption within the management but most approved of the decision to split into three divisions -- beer, China and softdrinks.
The news for Brierley Investments was mostly positive but a story in the Sydney Morning Herald that it may be the buyer of a 4.9 percent in retailer David Jones was viewed negatively by some.

Elsewhere, Williams & Kettle was down 12 cents to $1.91 while several smaller and thinly traded stocks had strong days including Radio Otago, Waste Management, Wang NZ and McCollam Printers. -- Simon Louisson 64 4 4734 746
